m:altstadt: Free to walk, at any hour. Shops close early in the evening and on Sundays almost all are closed (in Switzerland shops rest); restaurants and cafés stay open. On Saturday mornings in spring and summer there's a market on some squares.
m:grossmunster: From the Zurich Tourism website: the tower is open Monday to Saturday 10am–6pm from March to October and 10am–5pm from November to February; on Sundays it opens after the service, around 12:30pm. The climb costs CHF 5 (about €5.40), it's 187 steps and the terraces are closed for safety. From January 2025 to 2029 restoration work is under way on the church: some parts may be covered by scaffolding or closed.
m:fraumunster: From the Zurich Tourism website: entry costs CHF 5 (about €5.40), free for under-16s and students. Open Monday to Saturday 10am–6pm from March to October and 10am–5pm from November to February; on Sundays it opens after the service, around noon. The Chagall windows look best in the morning, with the sun coming from the east.
m:lindenhof: It's a square open to all, free, at any hour. Reach it from Rennweg or Schipfe up a short flight of steps.
m:bahnhofstrasse: Free to walk. Shops are normally open Monday to Saturday until 6:30–8pm and closed on Sundays (except at the main station, where Shopville is open every day, Sundays included).
m:landesmuseum: From the museum website: Tuesday–Sunday 10am–5pm, closed on Mondays. Entry CHF 13 (about €14), reduced CHF 10, free up to age 16 and with the Zürich Card. On 24 December it closes at 2pm.
m:kunsthaus: From the museum website: Tuesday, Wednesday and Friday to Sunday 10am–6pm, Thursday 10am–8pm, closed on Mondays. Collection and small exhibitions CHF 24 (about €25.70), reduced CHF 17; the collection is free every Wednesday. With a major exhibition the ticket goes up to CHF 31. Closed on 25 December and 1 January; on 24 and 31 December open 10am–4pm.
m:lago: The promenade is free and always open. The boats (ZSG) run a reduced timetable in October and even fewer sailings in winter: check times on zsg.ch. On Tuesday and Friday mornings there's a market on Bürkliplatz.
m:poly: The Polybahn is included in ZVV tickets; it runs during the day, every few minutes (times to be checked). The terrace is free, at any hour.
m:uetliberg: Go up on the S10 train from platform 21 or 22 at the main station (about two trains an hour, more at weekends); the «zone 110» day ticket isn't enough, because the station is outside the city zone: you need tickets for the extra zones (about CHF 7.20 for 3 zones, to be checked in the ZVV app). The observation tower has a ticket of CHF 2–5 depending on the period and the operator, to be checked on the spot. In snow or ice the path is slippery.
m:lindt: From the Zurich Tourism website: open every day 10am–7pm; adults CHF 17 (about €18.20), ages 8–15 CHF 10, children up to 7 free. Best to book a time slot online. The fountain, the shop and the café are accessible without a ticket. Hours and prices from the 2025 page: to be confirmed on the official website.
vd:zeughaus: A 15th-century former armoury near Paradeplatz, turned into a big wooden hall with long tables: old-fashioned Swiss cooking, with sausages, Zürcher Geschnetzeltes, Wiener schnitzel, cordon bleu and a sausage and cheese salad.
vp:zeughaus: A main course usually costs CHF 25–35 (about €27–37); it's the cheapest traditional place in the area (menu not seen). Hours from the Zurich Tourism website.
vd:spruengli: Zurich's most famous pâtisserie, open since 1836 on Paradeplatz: a room with little tables, chocolate, cakes and Luxemburgerli, the house's little macarons. The ground-floor café also serves breakfasts and light dishes.
vp:spruengli: A coffee with a slice of cake is around CHF 12–16; Luxemburgerli are sold by the piece, a few francs (menu not seen). Hours from the Zurich Tourism website.
vd:hiltl: The world's oldest vegetarian restaurant (since 1898): a buffet with over a hundred hot and cold dishes, paid by weight, and a rich breakfast. There are vegan options and choices for non-vegetarians too.
vp:hiltl: Paid by weight: a well-filled plate is usually around CHF 20–30; breakfast CHF 15–25 (menu not seen). Hours from the Zurich Tourism website.
vd:chuchi: A traditional Swiss restaurant in the heart of the Niederdorf, with a mountain-hut atmosphere: cheese fondue, raclette, Zürcher Geschnetzeltes with rösti and Alpine macaroni. It also serves a Swiss breakfast, with Bircher muesli, cheeses and cold cuts.
vp:chuchi: A fondue usually costs CHF 30–40 per person; a breakfast CHF 20–25 (menu not seen). Hours from the Zurich Tourism website.
vd:schober: A historic Niederdorf pâtisserie, with rooms lined in wood and velvet: the star of the house is hot chocolate with cream, with homemade cakes and pralines.
vp:schober: A hot chocolate with cream costs about CHF 8–10 and a slice of cake the same (menu not seen). Hours from a travel guide, to be confirmed.
vd:wolf: A big Bavarian-style beer hall along the Limmat, with huge steins and simple hot dishes: schnitzel, cordon bleu in various versions, spätzle and bratwurst, served with pretzels. Lively and noisy, with live music.
vp:wolf: A main course is usually around CHF 25–35 (menu not seen). Hours from the Zurich Tourism website.
vd:rheinfelder: A real Niederdorf beer hall, without the postcard tourists: generous portions of home-style Swiss cooking, like pork liver (Schweinsleberli), bratwurst, rösti and chnöpfli, and a gigantic cordon bleu, the house speciality.
vp:rheinfelder: Dishes at CHF 20–30, among the cheapest in the centre (menu not seen). The kitchen closes at 11:15pm; hours from an online guide, to be confirmed.
vd:oepfel: An 1801 tavern in a half-timbered house, with low wooden beams and the tradition of climbing onto a beam to drink a glass upside down. It serves Zurich dishes and seasonal specialities.
vp:oepfel: A dish is usually around CHF 25–40 (menu not seen). Closed on Mondays and Sundays; hours from the Zurich Tourism website.
vd:odeon: A historic 1912 café near Bellevue, with high ceilings, mirrors and a clientele of artists and students: breakfasts, coffee, cakes and simple dishes in a single room.
vp:odeon: A coffee with a slice of cake is around CHF 10–14; breakfast CHF 12–20 (menu not seen). Hours from the Zurich Tourism website (open until 2am on Fridays and Saturdays).
vd:sternen: The St Gallen bratwurst grill kiosk, always busy near Bellevue: the big, fat sausage is eaten with a crusty roll and mustard, standing or at little tables. Zurich's classic quick lunch.
vp:sternen: A bratwurst with bread is usually around CHF 8–11 (menu not seen). Hours from the Switzerland Tourism website: open Monday to Saturday, Sunday isn't listed; to be confirmed.
cd:zoozurigo: A zoo on the Zürichberg, with the Masoala rainforest.
cd:rietberg: Non-European art in a park, with a villa and a modern building.
cd:fifa: The history of world football and the World Cup trophy.
cd:lagocruise: A boat on the lake, among villas and vineyards.
cd:beyer: A collection of clocks and timekeeping instruments, on Bahnhofstrasse.
cd:cabaretvoltaire: The place where Dada was born in 1916.
